outcome.reasoning:
Nitpicks: Currency showing as EUR / delivery to Germany is not inherently a problem as long as the agent still correctly filters to < $40 equivalent and reports the required product fields; minor formatting like “13.1K” vs an exact number is also a nitpick.

Critical issues:
1) Missing required filters (Prime eligible and price < $40) with no valid justification. The agent explicitly states Prime and <$40 were “not visible or confirmed” and proceeds anyway, but the task required these constraints; there was no bot-check/access block forcing an early stop. Screenshots show normal access to results and sorting, so failure to apply/verify Prime + <$40 is a substantive miss.
2) Reported ‘top three’ products are not reliably the top three in the final sorted view and include likely fabricated/unsupported items. The latest screenshot (5) with sort set to “Avg. Customer Review” shows the first item as a Tourmate hard travel case (case only), and the second item as the Logitech Pebble Pink Rose. The agent instead reports Logitech Pebble Pink Rose as #1 and then lists an “INFINMIND L610...” and a Logitech Pebble Off White as #2/#3, neither of which is evidenced in the provided screenshots. This is a correctness failure for the primary deliverable (the three product records).
3) Even within the visible sorted list, the page appears to include non-mouse accessories (e.g., the #1 item is a travel case) and at least one wired mouse appears as #3 in screenshot 5; the agent did not successfully enforce the intended constraints that would keep results to relevant wireless mice meeting Prime + price requirements.

Outcome: The agent did successfully perform the search and did change the sort to Avg. Customer Review, but it did not complete the required filtering and did not produce three verifiably correct ‘top three’ product records under the required filtered+sorted conditions. From an average user’s perspective, the final deliverable (accurate top 3 items meeting all constraints) was not achieved.
outcome.primary_intent: The user wanted the agent to use Amazon to search for “wireless mouse”, then actually apply three hard constraints (≥4 stars rating, Prime eligible, and price below $40) and sort by average rating, and finally report the top 3 resulting products with title, price, rating, and review count. A reasonable user would be flexible about minor UI differences (e.g., exact wording of the sort) but not flexible about missing required filters or reporting items that aren’t demonstrably the top three under the specified filtered+sorted setup.
